DETAILED ACTION
Notice of Pre-AIA  or AIA  Status
The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA .
Drawings
The drawings are objected to under 37 CFR 1.83(b) because they are incomplete.  37 CFR 1.83(b) reads as follows:
When the invention consists of an improvement on an old machine the drawing must when possible exhibit, in one or more views, the improved portion itself, disconnected from the old structure, and also in another view, so much only of the old structure as will suffice to show the connection of the invention therewith.
The drawing shown in figures 1 – 9 merely show rectangles, squares and boxes as the invention and no does not show the full structure of the charging pile, interpreted as a charging station for electric vehicles. The rectangles and squares are not a flow chart and do not provide the full illustration of an embodiment of the invention. As a reference, using prior art reference Heyne as shown below, shows a flow chart description in figure 1 and then shows a real life embodiment of the invention in figure 2.
Corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment of the application. Any amended replacement drawing sheet should include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is being amended. The figure or figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as “amended.”  If a drawing figure is to be canceled, the appropriate figure must be removed from the replacement sheet, and where necessary, the remaining figures must be renumbered and appropriate changes made to the brief description of the several views of the drawings for consistency. Additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show the renumbering of the remaining figures. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of an application must be labeled in the top margin as either “Replacement Sheet” or “New Sheet” pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). If the changes are not accepted by the examiner, the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action. The objection to the drawings will not be held in abeyance.

Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 112
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112(b):
(b)  CONCLUSION.—The specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention.
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA ), second paragraph:
The specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the applicant regards as his invention.
Claim 11 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA ), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA  35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention.
Where applicant acts as his or her own lexicographer to specifically define a term of a claim contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the claim term and set forth the uncommon definition so as to put one reasonably skilled in the art on notice that the applicant intended to so redefine that claim term. Process Control Corp. v. HydReclaim Corp., 190 F.3d 1350, 1357, 52 USPQ2d 1029, 1033 (Fed. Cir. 1999).
The term “charging pile” in claims 1 – 20 is not standard English and should be changed to “charging station for electric vehicles”.
The term “setting mode” in claim 11 is used by the claim to mean “positioning within a charging station,” while the accepted meaning is “a charging setting mode, wherein a specific charging mode is set.” The term is indefinite because the specification does not clearly redefine the term.
A broad range or limitation together with a narrow range or limitation that falls within the broad range or limitation (in the same claim) may be considered indefinite if the resulting claim does not clearly set forth the metes and bounds of the patent protection desired. See MPEP § 2173.05(c). In the present instance, Claim 11 recites:
The broad recitation “the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution are respectively arranged at the top and bottom inside of the box.”
The narrower recitation, the claim also recites “the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are both arranged at the top or bottom inside of the box.”
The narrower recitation, the claim also recites, “one of the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit is located at front end of the power conversion unit and at the top inside of the box, and the other is located at the bottom inside of the box.”
The narrower recitation, the claim also recites, “one of the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit is located at the front end of the power conversion unit and arranged at the bottom inside of the box, and the other is located at the top inside of the box.”
The narrower recitation, the claim also recites, “the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are both located at the front end of the power conversion unit and are respectively located at the top and bottom inside of the box.”
It is unclear where the power distribution and AC power distribution is located within the charging pile. The claim(s) are considered indefinite because there is a question or doubt as to whether the feature introduced by such narrower language is (a) merely exemplary of the remainder of the claim, and therefore not required, or (b) a required feature of the claims.
Claims 3,11, 13, 17 and 18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA ), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA  35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention. The claims recite an “AC power distribution” and a “power distribution.” It is unclear how these two items are two separate devices or items within the system. The AC power distribution has been interpreted as an “input port” and the power distribution has been interpreted as an “output port.”
Where applicant acts as his or her own lexicographer to specifically define a term of a claim contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the claim term and set forth the uncommon definition so as to put one reasonably skilled in the art on notice that the applicant intended to so redefine that claim term. Process Control Corp. v. HydReclaim Corp., 190 F.3d 1350, 1357, 52 USPQ2d 1029, 1033 (Fed. Cir. 1999). The term “AC Power Distribution” in claims 3,11, 13, 17 and 18 is used by the claim to mean “an input port,” while the accepted meaning is “an input port.” The term is indefinite because the specification does not clearly redefine the term. The term “Power Distribution” in claims 2-4,12,17 and 18 is used by the claim to mean “an output port,” while the accepted meaning is “an output port.” The term is indefinite because the specification does not clearly redefine the term.
6.	Claim 4 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA ), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA  35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention. Claim 4, dependent upon claim 3 and further 1, states, “when the plurality of heating elements are arranged on a plurality of sides of the air-cooled radiator, each of the plurality of heating elements on different sides of the air-cooled radiator is connected by a cable in a sealed wire groove.” The claim is indefinite, because as structural claim, it is unclear as to “when” something may occur, either a surface of the liquid cooling radiator is cooling elements which are heated or it is stored in another location. The language, “placed” is unclear and appears to describe the cooling liquid flowing in a specific direction. It is unclear how the cooling radiator is “placed,” how it is “placed” and what devices are “placing” the cooling radiator. The claim has been interpreted to say, “when the cooling radiator is placed on a back plate of the box.”
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 102
The following is a quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for the rejections under this section made in this Office action:
A person shall be entitled to a patent unless –
(a)(2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application, as the case may be, names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
Claims 1 and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by Heyne (US 20190255961).
Regarding claim 1, Heyne teaches a charging pile (shown in figure 1 item 1 paragraph [0025] wherein a charging pile is interpreted as a charging station).
Heyne comprising: a charging unit (shown in figure 1 item 3 defined in paragraph [0024] as power electronics used for charging) and at least one air-cooled radiator, the charging unit and the at least one air-cooled radiator being arranged in a box of the charging pile, wherein (paragraph [0027] teaches blowers 12 may be arranged in the upper part of the charging station 10, which blowers provide a circulation of air in a region of the charging station 10 in which the condenser 14 of the cooling system is arranged).
Heyne teaches the box comprises a first box and a second box, a protection level of the first box is higher than a protection level of the second box; the charging unit is arranged in the first box (shown in figure 1 wherein the charging unit item 3 and cooling radiator, interpreted as a coolant reservoir are arranged in a box item 2 of the charging pile, interpreted as a charging station, item 1).
Heyne teaches wherein an independent heat dissipation air duct is provided in the second box so that the charging unit dissipates heat through the heat dissipation air duct (blowers 12 may be arranged in the upper part of the charging station 10, which blowers provide a circulation of air in a region of the charging station 10 in which the condenser 14 of the cooling system is arranged. The gaseous overheated coolant is cooled in the condenser 14).
Heyne teaches the charging unit is configured to charge an electrical equipment (shown in figure 1 item 3 defined in paragraph [0024] as power electronics used for charging).

Regarding claim 20, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 1, wherein the charging pile further comprises at least one charging gun arranged outside of the box, and the charging unit charges the electrical equipment through the charging gun (figure 1 shows a charging gun, interpreted as a charging connector item 5 for charging a vehicle).
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 103
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 103 which forms the basis for all obviousness rejections set forth in this Office action:
A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained, notwithstanding that the claimed invention is not identically disclosed as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.
1.	Claims 2 and 5 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Waffner (US 20200180457).
Regarding claim 2, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 1, but does not explicitly teach wherein the first box adopts a sealed design.
Waffner teaches wherein the first box adopts a sealed design (paragraph [0047] teaches wherein the box, interpreted as a charging column 4 and a ground foundation 6 are each formed as a hollow housing. The cable duct 12 is preferably led through the housing of the ground foundation 6 in a waterproof way. The interior of the housing of the ground foundation 6 is sealed against the interior of the housing of the column 4).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne reference with the power conversion system of the Waffner reference so that the station may be protected from water damage.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Waffner reference in paragraph [0047] wherein the housing structure is sealed to prevent moisture from damaging the charging station.
Regarding claim 5, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 1, but does not explicitly teach wherein the first box is provided with waterproof terminals at both the input end and the output end of the charging unit.
Waffner teaches wherein the first box is provided with waterproof terminals at both the input end and the output end of the charging unit (paragraph [0047] teaches wherein the box, interpreted as a charging column 4 and a ground foundation 6 are each formed as a hollow housing. The cable duct 12 is preferably led through the housing of the ground foundation 6 in a waterproof way. The interior of the housing of the ground foundation 6 is sealed against the interior of the housing of the column 4).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne reference with the power conversion system of the Waffner reference so that the station may be protected from water damage.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Waffner reference in paragraph [0047] wherein the housing structure is sealed to prevent moisture from damaging the charging station.
Claims 3,4,6,7,8,9, and 10, are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Tsukamoto (US 20190308519).
Regarding claim 3, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 1, wherein the charging unit comprises: an alternating current (AC) power distribution unit, a power distribution unit, and at least one power conversion unit (defined in paragraph [0024] wherein a power conversion unit is taught).
Heyne does not explicitly teach wherein, an input end of the AC power distribution unit is configured to be an input end of the charging unit for receiving AC power supply; an output end of the AC power distribution unit is connected to an AC side of the power conversion unit; a plurality of direct current (DC) sides of the power conversion unit are respectively connected to a plurality of input ends of the power distribution unit; and an output end of the power distribution unit is configured to be an output end of the charging unit.
Tsukamoto teaches wherein, an input end of the AC power distribution unit is configured to be an input end of the charging unit for receiving AC power supply; an output end of the AC power distribution unit is connected to an AC side of the power conversion unit; a plurality of direct current (DC) sides of the power conversion unit are respectively connected to a plurality of input ends of the power distribution unit; and an output end of the power distribution unit is configured to be an output end of the charging unit (figure 2 shows an AC Power Distribution Unit. Item 500 shows an AC power supply input to a conversion unit item 210 which output a DC current).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne reference with the power conversion system of the Tsukamoto reference so that the power may be provided to the electric vehicle system safely.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Tsukamoto reference in paragraph [0037] wherein the charging system provides a conversion system.
Regarding claim 4, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 3, wherein the power conversion unit comprises a plurality of heating elements, and when the plurality of heating elements are arranged on a plurality of sides of the air-cooled radiator (defined in paragraph [0025] wherein a coolant is stored in the coolant reservoir 4, which coolant is able to be used to cool the power electronics item 3. Paragraph [0027] teaches wherein by way of the first heat exchanger 13, heat is removed from the air heated by the power electronics inside the charging station 10 and transferred to the coolant) each of the plurality of heating elements on different sides of the air-cooled radiator is connected by a cable in a sealed wire groove (paragraph [0006] teaches wherein the tank is configured such that as heat-emitting elements, that is to say in particular the electrical and electronic components, transfer their heat to the tank wall).
Regarding claim 6, Hyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 1, wherein the air-cooled radiator comprises at least one heat dissipation plate and a fan; one side of the heat dissipation plate is arranged in the first box, and the other side of the heat dissipation plate is arranged in the second box; and the fan is configured to agitate the airflow in the heat dissipation air duct (paragraph [0027] teaches blowers 12 may be arranged in the upper part of the charging station 10, which blowers provide a circulation of air in a region of the charging station 10 in which the condenser 14 of the cooling system is arranged).
Regarding claim 7, Hyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 6, wherein the heat dissipation plate comprises a substrate and a heat exchanger; the substrate is configured to be a common boundary plate for the first box and the second box; one side of the heat exchanger is arranged on the substrate in the second box; the other side of the heat exchanger is provided with a heat dissipation fin (paragraph [0027] teaches blowers 12 may be arranged in the upper part of the charging station 10, which blowers provide a circulation of air in a region of the charging station 10 in which the condenser 14 of the cooling system is arranged).
Regarding claim 8, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 7, wherein the power conversion unit in the charging unit is provided on the substrate; or the power conversion unit in the charging unit sinks inside the heat exchanger (defined in paragraph [0024] wherein the charging station 1 furthermore includes power electronics 3, which use a necessary voltage conversion and possible current conversion to provide a charging current, by way of which an electric vehicle connected to the charging station 1 via a charging connector 5 is able to be charged. Figure 1 shows wherein the conversion unit, included with the power electronics is connected to the coolant reservoir. Paragraph [0027] teaches wherein the power electronics are thus cooled by way of liquid cooling and heat sinks are attached directly to components of the power electronics. The power electronics may additionally be cooled by way of a cooling plate 15).
Regarding claim 9, Hyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 6, wherein the fan is arranged at bottom or top of the heat dissipation plate in the second box (paragraph [0027] teaches blowers 12 may be arranged in the upper part of the charging station 10, which blowers provide a circulation of air in a region of the charging station 10 in which the condenser 14 of the cooling system is arranged).
Regarding claim 10, Hyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 6, wherein two heat dissipation plates are provided, and the two heat dissipation plates are parallel; or a plurality of heat dissipation plates are provided, and each of the plurality of heat dissipation plates forms a polygonal prism structure; and the heat dissipation air duct is arranged between each of the plurality of heat dissipation plates (Paragraph [0027] teaches wherein the power electronics are thus cooled by way of liquid cooling and heat sinks are attached directly to components of the power electronics. The power electronics may be cooled by way of a cooling plate 15
2.	Claim 11 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Tsukamoto (US 20190308519) as applied to claim 3 and in further view of Christen (US 20170088005).
Regarding claim 11, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 3, wherein a setting mode of the AC power distribution unit (figures 1 and 2 show wherein the electronics may be arranged within the charging pile) but does not explicitly teach the power distribution unit is any one of the following: the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are respectively arranged at top and bottom inside of the box; the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are both arranged at the top or bottom inside of the box; one of the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit is located at front end of the power conversion unit and at the top inside of the box, and the other one is located at the bottom inside of the box; one of the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit is located at the front end of the power conversion unit and arranged at the bottom inside of the box, and the other one is located at the top inside of the box; and the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are both located at the front end of the power conversion unit and are respectively located at the top and bottom inside of the box.
Christen teaches wherein the power distribution unit is any one of the following: the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are respectively arranged at top and bottom inside of the box; the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are both arranged at the top or bottom inside of the box; one of the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit is located at front end of the power conversion unit and at the top inside of the box, and the other is located at the bottom inside of the box; one of the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit is located at the front end of the power conversion unit and arranged at the bottom inside of the box, and the other is located at the top inside of the box; and the power distribution unit and the AC power distribution unit are both located at the front end of the power conversion unit and are respectively located at the top and bottom inside of the box (shown in figure 2 wherein an AC power distribution port, shown wherein the external power source item 42 inputs power to the controller item 36 of the charging station item 32. A power distribution unit is located also on the bottom and may output power to the vehicle via item 38).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the port system of the Christen system so that the vehicle may be easily charged from the station.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Christen reference in paragraph [0004] wherein the vehicle may be easily charged.
3.	Claims 12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over in view of over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Tsukamoto (US 20190308519) in view of Christen (US 20170088005) as applied to claim 11 and in further view of Gotz (US 20180162229).
Regarding claim 12, Heyne in view of Tsukamoto teaches the charging pile according to claim 2, but does not explicitly teach wherein the power conversion unit comprises: one rectifier module and n DC/DC converters, where n is an integer greater than 1; an AC side of the rectifier module is configured to be as an input end of the power conversion unit; a DC side of the rectifier module is connected to input ends of the n DC/DC converters respectively; and output ends of the n DC/DC converters are respectively configured to be output ends of the power conversion unit.
Gotz teaches wherein the power conversion unit comprises: one rectifier module and n DC/DC converters, where n is an integer greater than 1; an AC side of the rectifier module is configured to be as an input end of the power conversion unit; a DC side of the rectifier module is connected to input ends of the n DC/DC converters respectively; and output ends of the n DC/DC converters are respectively configured to be output ends of the power conversion unit (figure 1 shows rectifier modules item 16 which are connected to DCDC converters item 26. Figures 2a-2b shows rectifier modules item 220 output to DCDC converters item 210).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the phase charging system of the Gotz reference so that the if the system fails, it is easy to repair.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Gotz reference in paragraph [0038] easily repairing the system is taught.
Claims 13-16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Tsukamoto (US 20190308519) as applied to claim 3 and in further view of Gotz (US 20180162229) and in further view of Asakura (US 20120181990).
Regarding claim 13, Heyne and Tsukamoto teaches the charging pile according to claim 12, but does not explicitly teach wherein the switch unit comprises: a drive circuit and an AC relay group; input ends of the AC relay group are connected to the input ends of the switch unit; output ends of the AC relay group are connected to the output ends of the switch unit.
Gotz teaches wherein the switch unit comprises: a drive circuit and an AC relay group; input ends of the AC relay group are connected to the input ends of the switch unit; output ends of the AC relay group are connected to the output ends of the switch unit (shown in figure 2b wherein a relay group is interpreted as switching elements item 222).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the phase charging system of the Gotz reference so that the if the system fails, it is easy to repair.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Gotz reference in paragraph [0038] easily repairing the system is taught.
Heyne, Tsukamoto in view of Gotz do not explicitly teach wherein the AC relay group is controlled by the drive circuit.
Asakura teaches the AC relay group is controlled by the drive circuit (shown in figure 1 wherein relay circuits items 46 and 53 are controlled by a drive circuit, interpreted as control unit item 54).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne, Tsukamoto and Gotz reference with the relay circuit controlled by a controller so that the vehicles may be charged more efficiently
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Asakura reference in paragraph [0046] the vehicles are charged more efficiently.
Regarding claim 14, Heyne in view of Tsukamoto teaches the charging pile according to claim 13, but does not explicitly teach wherein the AC relay group comprises: switch subunits respectively arranged on each phase cable in the AC relay group.
Gotz teaches wherein the AC relay group comprises: switch subunits respectively arranged on each phase cable in the AC relay group (figures 11a-11b show switch subunits arranged on each phase cable).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the phase charging system of the Gotz reference so that the if the system fails, it is easy to repair.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Gotz reference in paragraph [0038] easily repairing the system is taught.
Regarding claim 15, Heyne in view of Tsukamoto teaches the charging pile according to claim 14, but does not explicitly teach wherein at least one switch subunit comprises at least one relay.
Gotz teaches wherein at least one switch subunit comprises at least one relay (figures 11a-11b show switch subunits arranged on each phase cable).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the phase charging system of the Gotz reference so that the if the system fails, it is easy to repair.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Gotz reference in paragraph [0038] easily repairing the system is taught.
Regarding claim 16, Heyne, Tsukamoto in view of Gotz teaches the charging pile according to claim 13, but does not explicitly teach wherein the switch unit further comprises a circuit breaker; the circuit breaker is arranged between the input ends of the switch unit and the input ends of the AC relay group.
Asakura teaches wherein the switch unit further comprises a circuit breaker; the circuit breaker is arranged between the input ends of the switch unit and the input ends of the AC relay group (shown in figure 1 wherein the ground-fault circuit breakers ELB are provided between the power source devices 2 and the charging circuit 4).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the phase charging system of the Gotz reference so that the if the system fails, it is easy to repair.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Gotz reference in paragraph [0038] easily repairing the system is taught.
Claim 17 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Tsukamoto (US 20190308519) and in further view of Gotz (US 20180162229) and in further view of Asakura (US 20120181990) as applied to claim 13 and in further view of Sugano (US 20160121735).
Regarding claim 17, Heyne, Tsukamoto, Gotz and Asakura teaches the charging pile according to claim 13, but does not explicitly teach wherein the AC power distribution unit further comprises a lightning arrester; the A, B, and C three-phase inputs of the AC power supply are grounded through the lightning arrester.
Sugano teaches wherein the AC power distribution unit further comprises a lightning arrester; the A, B, and C three-phase inputs of the AC power supply are grounded through the lightning arrester (defined in paragraph [0072] wherein the charging station with an AC power distribution is grounded with a lightning arrester).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne, Tsukamoto in view of Gotz reference with the lightning arrester of the Sugano reference so that the charging station is protected from lighting damage.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Sugano reference in paragraph [0072] wherein the charging station is protected from lightning.
Claim 18 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Tsukamoto (US 20190308519) as applied to claim 3 and in further view of Asakura (US 20120181990).
Regarding claim 18, Heyne teaches the charging pile according to claim 2, wherein the charging unit further comprises a centralized control unit, (shown in figure 1 item 3 defined in paragraph [0024] wherein power electronics 3 are arranged in the charging station 1, power electronics being understood to mean the combination of all of the electrical and electronic components that are involved in providing energy from the buffer storage device 2 and/or the mains connection in order to charge an electric vehicle).
Heyne in view of Tsukamoto does not explicitly teach and the centralized control unit is configured to: send a first control signal to the AC power distribution unit to enable the AC power distribution unit to switch on and off; send a pulse width modulation (PWM) signal to the power conversion unit to enable the power conversion unit to implement electric energy conversion; and, send a second control signal to the power distribution unit to enable the power distribution unit to implement distribution of output power.
Asakura teaches the centralized control unit is configured to: send a first control signal to the AC power distribution unit to enable the AC power distribution unit to switch on and off; send a pulse width modulation (PWM) signal to the power conversion unit to enable the power conversion unit to implement electric energy conversion; and, send a second control signal to the power distribution unit to enable the power distribution unit to implement distribution of output power (shown in figures 1 and 10 wherein a centralized control unit item 54 and 354 provides control signals to AC power distribution and PWM signals as defined in paragraph [0089]).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the phase charging system of the Gotz reference so that the if the system fails, it is easy to repair.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Gotz reference in paragraph [0038] easily repairing the system is taught.
Claim 19 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Heyne (US 20190255961) in view of Tsukamoto (US 20190308519) as applied to claim 3 and in further view of Stocker (US 20180272886)
Regarding claim 19, Heyne in view of Tsukamoto teaches the charging pile according to claim 2, but does not explicitly teach wherein the charging unit further comprises a distributed control unit; the distributed control unit comprises a system controller and multiple sub-controllers; and each of the sub-controllers is respectively connected to the system controller in communication.
Stocker teaches wherein the charging unit further comprises a distributed control unit; the distributed control unit comprises a system controller and multiple sub-controllers; and each of the sub-controllers is respectively connected to the system controller in communication (paragraph [0133] teaches wherein sub controllers are used within the system).
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the charging system of the Heyne in view of Tsukamoto reference with the subcontroller system of the Stocker reference so that communication is more efficient with the charging station.
The suggestion/motivation for combination can be found in the Stocker reference in paragraph [0133] wherein subcontrollers provide more efficient charging.
